subject: environmental-science
title: Biodiversity & Wildlife: Threats
welcome_lead: Habitat loss, hunting and climate change all squeeze wildlife.
meta_desc: KS3 environmental science: extinction, deforestation, climate.
final_note: Once a species is gone, it is gone forever.

concepts.def: When a species dies out forever.
At high risk of going extinct.

walkthroughs.body_html: Deforestation for farms and cities removes habitats. With nowhere to live, populations crash and species become endangered.
Poaching — illegal hunting — has wiped out rhinos, elephants and tigers in some areas. Demand for tusks and skins drives it.
Warmer seas and changing seasons push species to move or adapt. Many can't keep up.

mcqs.q: Roughly what proportion of energy passes from one trophic level to the next?
How does the Brundtland Report define sustainable development?
options: Richness is for plants, evenness for animals.
Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between species richness and species evenness?
options: Richness is for plants, evenness for animals.
Richness counts how many species exist; evenness measures how balanced their abundances are.
